target.title: fix(cli): clean up abandoned egress opens to prevent conn+goroutine leak
target.body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** `egressBridge.openRemote` returned on timeout/cancel without deleting `pending[id]` or telling the host to close.
- **Why it matters:** two leaks on the long-lived client bridge — (1) the `pending` map grows unbounded when the host never replies; (2) a host reply that arrives after the timeout leaves the host's destination TCP conn and its `copyConnToBridge` goroutine alive for the life of the bridge.
- **What changed:**
  - `openRemote` drops the `pending` entry on timeout/cancel (`abandonOpen`).
  - `finishOpen` now reports whether a pending open still existed; a late `open_ok` for an already-abandoned id makes `clientReadLoop` tell the host to close.
  - the timeout-vs-reply race (`finishOpen` winning the moment `openRemote` gives up) is handled by draining the buffered result and closing on success.
  - both host-close writes are asynchronous with a detached, `egressDialTimeout`-bounded context, so they never stall the single `clientReadLoop` goroutine or block a canceling `openRemote`.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** the host-side (`hostOpen`/`copyConnToBridge`), `writeConn`/`closeConn`, and the success path are untouched. No protocol change — a `close` for an unknown id is already a no-op on the host.
- **AI-assisted:** yes (Claude); found via a concurrency audit (`signalkrebs`), verified manually and hardened across several independent reviews.

Part of openclaw/crabbox#1096.

## What to review
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/cli/egress.go` | abandon-cleanup + reactive close + race-safe settle + async bounded host-close |
| `internal/cli/egress_openremote_leak_test.go` | regression test (real client path + fake host over a websocket) |

## Real-behavior proof (base vs HEAD, exact revisions)
```
# base 808d96f
$ go test -race -run TestEgressOpenRemoteTimeoutLeaksPendingAndNeverClosesHostConn ./internal/cli/
--- FAIL: ... pending[id] leaked after openRemote timeout; host never received a "close" for the abandoned id
# HEAD
$ go test -race -run TestEgressOpenRemoteTimeoutLeaksPendingAndNeverClosesHostConn ./internal/cli/   -> ok (~22s)
$ go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test -race ./internal/cli/                                    -> ok
```
The test takes ~20s because it waits out the real `egressOpenTimeout` to hit the exact `timer.C` branch; it is `testing.Short()`-gated.

## What was NOT tested
No live mediated-egress session against a real remote host was run; the leak is exercised deterministically by driving the real client path (`connectEgressBridge` + `clientReadLoop` + `openRemote`) against a fake host over a real websocket.

## Regression test plan
`TestEgressOpenRemoteTimeoutLeaksPendingAndNeverClosesHostConn` asserts the two cleanup behaviours a correct implementation must have: (a) after a timed-out open, `pending[id]` is gone; (b) the host receives a `close` for the abandoned id (proactively or in response to a late `open_ok`). Both FAIL on base and PASS with the fix.

## Risks
- Risk: closing the host conn from the read loop or the cancel path could block or deadlock the bridge.
  - Mitigation: both host-close writes are `go`-dispatched with a detached, time-bounded context; the single read loop and `openRemote` never block on them. The `finishOpen`/`abandonOpen` mutex guarantees exactly one path sends the `close`, and the buffered channel guarantees the drain never blocks. Verified under `-race` and across independent reviews.

## Root cause
- **Symbol/file:** `egressBridge.openRemote`, `internal/cli/egress.go`.
- **Missing guardrail:** the abandon (timeout/cancel) path performed no cleanup — no `pending` delete, no host `close`.
- **Already correct:** the success path (`finishOpen`) and host side were fine.

## Security impact
- Auth/authorization path change? **No**
- Exposes a credential/secret? **No**
- Changes a trust boundary or network surface? **No** (only tears down conns *earlier*)
- Resource cleanup/lifetime in a security-relevant way? **Yes — fixes conn/goroutine/map leaks; no new exposure**
- Parses untrusted input in a new way? **No**

target.title: fix(cli): stop shadowing the WebVNC reconnect attempt counter
target.body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** in `serveWebVNCBridgeSlot`, the error branch used `attempt, kind := nextWebVNCBridgeFailure(connectedOnce, attempt)` — the `:=` declared a *new* `attempt` scoped to the `if` block, shadowing the loop's counter.
- **Why it matters:** `nextWebVNCBridgeFailure` increments and returns `attempt`, but the shadowed value was discarded, so the loop counter stayed at its initial value across consecutive connect failures. The reconnect backoff (`webVNCReconnectDelay(attempt)`) therefore never grew past its first-attempt delay — hammering the coordinator on a persistently-failing slot — and the failure `kind` never advanced past `initial-error`.
- **What changed:** declare `kind` separately and use `=`, so `attempt` is the loop counter and advances `1, 2, 3, …`.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `nextWebVNCBridgeFailure`, `webVNCReconnectDelay`, and the pool/event handling are untouched — this only stops the counter from being discarded.
- **AI-assisted:** yes (Claude); found via a concurrency audit (`signalkrebs`), verified manually and reviewed.

Part of openclaw/crabbox#1096.

## What to review
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/cli/webvnc.go` | `:=` → declared `kind` + `=` so `attempt` updates the loop counter |
| `internal/cli/webvnc_backoff_shadow_test.go` | regression test |

## Real-behavior proof (base vs HEAD)
```
# base 808d96f
$ go test -race -run TestWebVNCBridgeSlotBacksOffAcrossConnectFailures ./internal/cli/
--- FAIL: ... failure 2: Attempt=1, want 2 (attempt counter lost: shadowed by := ; backoff pinned)
# HEAD
$ go test -race -run TestWebVNCBridgeSlotBacksOffAcrossConnectFailures ./internal/cli/   -> ok
$ go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test -race ./internal/cli/                         -> ok
```

## What was NOT tested
No live WebVNC bridge against a real coordinator; the counter/backoff progression is exercised deterministically by driving `serveWebVNCBridgeSlot` through repeated connect failures.

## Regression test plan
The test drives consecutive connect failures and asserts the emitted `Attempt` advances (1, 2, 3, …) and the failure kind transitions correctly. FAILS on base (Attempt stuck at 1), PASSES with the fix.

## Risks
- Risk: changing scoping could alter the emitted `kind`/`attempt` semantics.
  - Mitigation: `kind` is assigned identically; only the counter's persistence changes, which is the intended fix. Verified by the test and reviewed.

## Root cause
- **Symbol/file:** `serveWebVNCBridgeSlot`, `internal/cli/webvnc.go`.
- **Missing guardrail:** a `:=` where `=` was intended, silently shadowing a loop variable (no compiler warning).
- **Already correct:** `nextWebVNCBridgeFailure` and the backoff schedule were fine.

## Security impact
- Auth/authorization path change? **No**
- Exposes a credential/secret? **No**
- Changes a trust boundary or network surface? **No** (reduces coordinator hammering)
- Resource cleanup/lifetime in a security-relevant way? **No**
- Parses untrusted input in a new way? **No**

target.title: fix(cli): stop telemetry sampler on failed runs to prevent goroutine leak
target.body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** `runRecorder.Failed` marks the run finished but, unlike `Finish`, never calls `stopTelemetrySampler`. `Finish` stops the sampler; `Failed` does not.
- **Why it matters:** the telemetry sampler goroutine and its ticker leak on **every failed run**, continuing to SSH-probe the already-released lease until the process's root context dies. A long-lived CLI (bench loops, multi-run sessions) accumulates one leaked goroutine + ticker per failure.
- **What changed:** call `r.stopTelemetrySampler()` in `Failed`, right after `r.finished = true` — the same placement `Finish` uses.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `Finish`, `StartTelemetrySampler`, `stopTelemetrySampler`, and the event/coordinator paths are untouched. `stopTelemetrySampler` is idempotent (nils `telemetryCancel`/`telemetryDone` under the mutex, early-returns if already stopped), and `Failed`/`Finish` are mutually exclusive (both guard on `r.finished`), so no double-stop or ordering hazard.
- **AI-assisted:** yes (Claude); found via a concurrency audit (`signalkrebs`), failing test + fix verified manually.

Part of openclaw/crabbox#1096.

## What to review
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/cli/run_recorder.go` | `Failed` now stops the telemetry sampler (mirrors `Finish`) |
| `internal/cli/run_recorder_telemetry_leak_test.go` | regression test |

## Real-behavior proof (base vs HEAD, exact revisions)
```
# base 808d96f (leak present)
$ go test -race -run TestFailedStopsTelemetrySampler -count=1 ./internal/cli/
--- FAIL: TestFailedStopsTelemetrySampler
    goroutine leak: telemetry sampler still running after runRecorder.Failed marked the run finished; Failed never calls stopTelemetrySampler, unlike Finish

# HEAD (fixed)
$ go test -race -run TestFailedStopsTelemetrySampler -count=1 ./internal/cli/   -> ok
$ go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test -race ./internal/cli/               -> ok (221s)
```

## What was NOT tested
No live multi-run CLI session against a real coordinator+lease was run. The leak is exercised deterministically by the unit test driving the real `StartTelemetrySampler` → `Failed` sequence and polling `runtime.NumGoroutine` back to baseline, so a live run is not needed to prove it.

## Regression test plan
`TestFailedStopsTelemetrySampler` starts a real telemetry sampler, calls `Failed`, and asserts the sampler goroutine returns to baseline within a deadline (dumping the leaked stack on failure). It FAILS on base (goroutine survives) and PASSES with the fix. Smallest reliable guardrail: the bug is a missing-cleanup on one code path, so a unit test that drives that exact path and counts goroutines pins it directly.

## Risks
- Risk: stopping the sampler in `Failed` could race the sampler goroutine or double-stop.
  - Mitigation: `stopTelemetrySampler` is mutex-guarded and idempotent; `Failed`/`Finish` are mutually exclusive via the `r.finished` guard. Verified under `-race`.

## Root cause
- **Symbol/file:** `runRecorder.Failed`, `internal/cli/run_recorder.go`.
- **Missing guardrail:** the failure path omitted the sampler-stop that the success path (`Finish`) performs.
- **Already correct:** `Finish` and `stopTelemetrySampler` were fine; only `Failed` was missing the call.

## Security impact
- Auth/authorization path change? **No**
- Exposes a credential/secret? **No**
- Changes a trust boundary or network surface? **No** (stops an unwanted probe *earlier*, if anything reduces surface)
- Resource cleanup/lifetime in a security-relevant way? **Yes — fixes a resource (goroutine/ticker) leak; no new exposure**
- Parses untrusted input in a new way? **No**

target.title: docs: add Features capability explorer
target.body:
## Summary

- Reframe the Features index around reusable capabilities rather than providers or command syntax.
- Replace the long generated Markdown list with a polished, responsive capability explorer on `/features/`.
- Add a strong product-oriented hero, a Lease → Sync → Run → Prove flow, live search, category filters, result counts, and linked capability cards.
- Keep provider discovery in the canonical Provider Reference and command syntax in the Command Reference.
- Preserve every existing feature document and URL; the enhancement runs after the normal docs build and only transforms the Features landing page.

## Why

The docs now give Providers a first-class section, but the Features landing page still behaved like a dense Markdown inventory and duplicated adjacent information architecture. It was technically complete but difficult to scan, did not communicate the product workflow, and made dozens of capability guides feel flat and undifferentiated.

This change gives `/features/` one clear job: help a reader understand what Crabbox can do and quickly find the relevant capability contract.

## UX and accessibility

- Responsive three-, two-, and one-column card layouts.
- Searchable capability titles and descriptions.
- Filter pills for each capability area, with pressed state and live result counts.
- Keyboard-friendly native links, buttons, labels, and search input.
- Escape clears an active search.
- Empty-result status is announced and category sections hide only when they have no visible cards.
- Existing light/dark theme variables and reduced-motion behavior remain authoritative.
- Provider and command CTAs create an explicit handoff to the correct top-level section.

## Implementation

The shared Markdown renderer remains unchanged. `scripts/enhance-docs-site.mjs` deterministically post-processes only `dist/docs-site/features/index.html` after the normal build. This isolates the richer landing-page treatment from all other documentation pages and avoids committing generated output.

The Pages workflow and `scripts/check-docs.sh` both run the enhancement, so CI validates the same output that is deployed.

## Visual proof

The `Docs UI Proof / Render visual proof` check builds the exact generated docs output from the PR head, runs the enhancer and regression tests, and renders browser screenshots with pinned Playwright/Chromium.

Its downloadable artifact is named `features-ui-proof-<head-sha>` and contains:

- `features-desktop-light.png` — full desktop layout in light mode.
- `features-desktop-dark.png` — full desktop layout using the dark color scheme.
- `features-mobile.png` — full responsive mobile layout using an iPhone viewport.
- `SHA256SUMS` — digests binding each proof image to the workflow artifact.

The proof job also fails unless the generated page contains the capability explorer, product hero, provider handoff, and command-reference handoff. This makes the evidence reproducible rather than a manually edited screenshot.

## Validation

- `node --check scripts/enhance-docs-site.mjs`
- `node --test scripts/enhance-docs-site.test.mjs`
- Enhancer regression coverage verifies the hero, search/filter surface, capability-card generation, TOC/pager removal, idempotence, and no-op behavior for unrelated pages.
- `Docs UI Proof / Render visual proof` publishes desktop light, desktop dark, and mobile screenshots from the exact built PR output.
- Branch is based directly on upstream `main` (`6da7760693a820c53434b4774077f526d362c136`) with no unrelated files.

Generated site output remains uncommitted.
